narrative.overview:
This is a portfolio where the work does the talking. The visual system is dark, warm, and uncluttered — not because dark is fashionable, but because it sets conditions for text and work to surface without interference. A near-black with an amber undertone (Forge, #1c1813) reads as heated iron rather than cold slate. The single accent — a muted amber-gold (Ember, #d4a020) — functions like a highlighter pen: used rarely, and always with intent.

The typography is confident without being showy. Space Grotesk brings geometric character to headings without tipping into editorial performance; Inter handles body copy with clinical precision. Together they read as someone who chose deliberately, not someone who overthought it.

The design does not beg for attention. A recruiter opening this page should feel: 'This person knows what they're doing' — not through visual tricks, but through an absence of them.
keyCharacteristics: Warm dark mode: amber undertones in every neutral, no cold blue-black
Single accent (Ember) used parsimoniously — it marks load-bearing elements only
Flat surfaces, border-first depth — no decorative shadows
Space Grotesk + Inter: geometric confidence at heading scale, functional precision at body scale
672px reading column: comfortable at any viewport, never stretched

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Ember (#d4a020) appears on at most 15% of any screen. It marks section labels, company names, primary CTAs, and title hover states. If you find yourself adding Ember to a second category, remove it from an existing one first.

rules.name: The Warm Neutrals Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system is a cool gray. Every background, border, and muted tone is tinted toward H=50-75. A neutral like #6b7280 (Tailwind's gray-500) is a contamination of the palette.

rules.name: The No-Scale-Collapse Rule
rules.body: The step between Label (11px), Body (15px), Title (16px), Headline (30px), and Display (48px+) must always be 1.25 or greater between adjacent levels. Never add an intermediate size.

rules.name: The Label Doctrine
rules.body: Section eyebrows are the only uppercase text on the site. No other element uses text-transform: uppercase. Uppercase is a limited resource — spend it in one place or it means nothing anywhere.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: At rest, every element is flat. Shadows appear only in response to state (locked navbar) or genuine structural hierarchy. Cards, sections, and content regions are never lifted.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Before reaching for a shadow, ask: does a border, background tint, or spacing increase solve the same problem? Use that first.

dos: Do use Ember (#d4a020) exclusively for section eyebrow labels, company names in experience cards, the primary CTA button, and project title hover states.
Do keep every neutral warm. All background, border, and text tones carry H=50-75 with at least 0.005 chroma.
Do cap all body and description text at 72ch.
Do set the hero name in Space Grotesk 700 with -0.03em letter-spacing.
Do use border tinting and background shifts before reaching for shadows.
Do keep all project and experience cards at one visual weight.
donts: Don't use indigo, violet, or blue-purple as an accent. The current indigo-600 (#4f46e5) must be migrated to Ember.
Don't use neon or glowing accents, frosted glass panels used decoratively, or high-chroma colors on dark backgrounds.
Don't copy the Linear or Vercel palette directly. Warm amber is intentionally distinct from their cold-slate and violet accent.
Don't let Ember appear on more than 15% of any screen.
Don't use pure white (#ffffff) or pure black (#000000).
Don't add progress bars, skill meters, or percentage counters.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on any card or list item.
Don't add cool grays from Tailwind's default slate palette without re-tinting toward H=50-75.
